summary: Parameters pass values into a function, and return sends a result back. Use return when the caller needs the answer, not just printed text.
notes: points = 5 is a default. curve(72) uses 5 and curve(98, 10) uses 10.
summarize() returns one array. const [low, high, average] = ... unpacks it into 3 variables.
Math.min(...scores) spreads the array into separate arguments, because Math.min() takes numbers, not an array.
pitfall: Writing return alone on a line with the array on the next line returns undefined, because JavaScript ends the statement right after return. Start the value on the same line as return.
contrast: Like Python, JavaScript has default parameter values (points = 5), so it needs no overloading as Java does. A function returns one value, but returning an array and unpacking it with const [low, high, average] works like Python's tuple.
